extracted.intended_audience: scientists, medical professionals, and educated lay readers of Popular Science Monthly
extracted.subtask_description: Short evaluative notices of recently published scientific books, reports, and journals assessing their scholarship, style, usefulness, and suitability for particular audiences (e.g., practitioners, students, researchers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Thoroughness and careful observation
rubrics_metrics.description: Works should show careful observation and painstaking labor and may be judged trustworthy and authoritative on that basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example wording: Evans's Stone Implements was 'a monument of careful observation and painstaking labor' and was 'accepted as a trustworthy and authoritative work.' Value is placed on accumulation of a large mass of facts for comparative archaeology to succeed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality, quantity, and execution of illustrations
rubrics_metrics.description: Illustrations should be numerous, well chosen, and well executed, enhancing the reader's understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judd's volume praised because 'the illustrations are numerous, well chosen, and especially fine in execution.' The presence of plates/photographs supporting data (e.g., 27 plates, photographs of septic organisms) is noted as a merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and lucidity of writing/presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: The author should present material lucidly and be a skilled, agreeable writer; clarity of statement is a major virtue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Praises such as 'very agreeable writer' and 'master of the art of statement' (Judd) indicate high value on lucid exposition; works 'set forth clearly and in detail' are commended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation of current research / being up-to-date
rubrics_metrics.description: A journal or book should 'thoroughly represent the advance of research' in its field and have high claims upon professionals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Journal of Physiology is noted for representing the advance of research; this supports its claim on the medical profession and those interested in physiological science.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical grounding: reliance on observation and experiment
rubrics_metrics.description: The principal object should be presentation of results attained by observation and experiment; theoretical discussion should be subordinated to empirical results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judd: 'I have endeavored...to give an account of those investigations which have in recent times thrown so much fresh light... While not evading theoretical questions, I have endeavored to keep such discussions in strict subordination to...observation and experiment.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of representative examples and deduction of general laws
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should select examples that are truly typical and use them to deduce general laws governing the phenomena discussed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judd explains: 'I have confined myself to the examination of such selected examples of volcanoes as could be shown to be really typical... and I have endeavored from the study of these to deduce those general laws.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and breadth of standpoint
rubrics_metrics.description: A work may be judged by its willingness to approach topics from new standpoints or to dwell on subjects not immediately germane if they illuminate the main question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judd intentionally 'approach[es] the question from a somewhat new standpoint' and discusses topics (e.g., microscopic characters of lavas, relations to meteorites) that broaden understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of detailed typology/minor details for comparative studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Minute, seemingly unimportant details in form and character may provide valuable evidence and clues for tracing cultural or biological descent; detailed typology is valuable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evans: minor differences in implements 'may, to a skillful archaeologist, afford valuable clews by which the march of the bronze civilization over Europe can be traced.' Accumulating large masses of such facts is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical utility for intended professional audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Books prepared for practitioners should address anatomy/examination/methods/medication, include case descriptions, and be practically applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coomes' Naso-Pharyngeal Catarrh is 'a practical treatise for the use of general practitioners' treating anatomy, examination, methods of local and constitutional medication, and many case descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagnostic clarity and evidence of treatment outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Medical works should provide clear diagnosis criteria and report methods and results of treatment (including cases) so clinicians can assess effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shaffer's Hysterical Element volume 'gives the diagnosis of such cases, with accounts of the method and results of treatment.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental detail, methodological transparency, and supporting imagery
rubrics_metrics.description: Experimental researches should describe experiments in detail and provide photographic/microscopic images of organisms or results to support findings and reproducibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sternberg's experimental research: 'The experiments are described in detail, and photographs of the septic organisms developed after the injections are also given.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear research objectives and graphical/quantitative presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports should state clear objectives (e.g., ascertain composition/optimum harvest time) and present results graphically and quantitatively where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collier's report aimed 'to ascertain as many facts as possible' and 'experiments were generally directed to the demonstration of the period at which the juice...contained the most crystallizable sugar'; 'Large sheet plates present graphically the results of 3,601 analyses.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical/applied value and organized, classified presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Works describing industrial or applied advances should be rich in instructive facts valuable for practical application and present processes in classified detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mallet's review: 'full of instructive facts, valuable for practical application... the improved chemical processes and applications which it describes in classified detail.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational coherence and structural integration
rubrics_metrics.description: A book's parts should be well connected; disjointed divisions that leave readers 'in doubt as to their connection' are a structural fault.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Brunton's Bible and Science: 'The method of the book is somewhat novel. It is divided into two parts, which are so separate and so different that the reader is left long in doubt as to their connection.' This is presented as a critique of coherence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pedagogical value: ability to awaken interest and provide practical instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: Works intended to teach should awaken interest, assist intelligent observation, include appendices with practical instructions (collecting, rearing, preserving), and provide bibliographies/systematic lists to facilitate study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scudder's Butterflies: 'intended to awaken interest in the study... to assist in intelligent observation' and includes an appendix with 'instructions for collecting, rearing, preserving... the bibliography...and a systematic list.'
